headline: US Central Command Facilitates 1.5 Billion Barrels of Oil Exports via Hormuz
summary: U.S. Central Command stated it helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz since summer, bypassing an Iranian blockade.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical maritime chokepoint for global energy supplies, and any disruption or military intervention directly impacts global crude oil pricing and trade flows.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Successful naval escorts and bypassed blockades normalize oil transit flows, reducing supply-disruption risk premiums.

why_moved: Assurances of secure passage through a vital oil transit corridor reduce geopolitical risk premiums embedded in petroleum futures.
